title: Story Parts
objectives: I can tell the setting of a story.
I can tell an event and the solution in a story.
I can tell what a story's lesson is.
I can imagine and tell my own adventure.
rationale: These words let first graders say where, what, and how a story works. Setting, event, and solution name three parts of every story children read, adventure names the kind of story they love, lesson names what a story teaches, and imagine names what they do when they make up their own. The unit builds on the order and cause words from earlier (then, finally, happen), since an event comes after another event and a solution follows a problem.

words.def: Where and when a story takes place.
words.ex: The setting of the story is a farm in summer.
words.ex2: A dark forest is the setting for the scary story.
words.nonExample: A character's name is not the setting.

apps.academic: Tell the setting before you tell the events.
apps.writing: Name the setting at the start of your story.

cloze.s: The ___ of the story is a snowy mountain in winter.

cloze2.s: In my story, the ___ is a beach on a hot, sunny day.

misuse.s: The setting of the story was a boy named Leo.
misuse.why: A setting is a place and time. A boy is a character.

visual.alt: A snowy mountain next to an open book.

words.def: A thing that happens, like a party.
words.ex: The class picnic was a fun event.
words.ex2: The big event in the story was a flood.
words.nonExample: A tree standing still is not an event.

apps.writing: Use first, next, and last to write each event.

cloze.s: The school play is a big ___ that everyone comes to see.

cloze2.s: First, the dog ran away. That was the first ___ in the story.

misuse.s: The event was a red hat on a table.
misuse.why: An event is something that happens. A hat sitting on a table does not happen.

visual.alt: Party decorations beside a calendar page.

words.def: The way a problem gets fixed.
words.ex: The solution to the mess was a mop.
words.ex2: Their solution for the lost cat was to put up signs.
words.nonExample: A problem is not the solution; it needs one.

apps.academic: Find the problem and the solution in the story.
apps.writing: Tell how the character solved the problem.

cloze.s: The cat was stuck in the tree, and the ___ was a tall ladder.

cloze2.s: Mia found a ___ to the puzzle when she turned the last piece.

misuse.s: The solution to the broken toy was to break it more.
misuse.why: A solution fixes a problem. Breaking the toy more makes it worse.

visual.alt: A puzzle piece fitting into place with a light bulb.

words.def: An exciting trip where new things happen.
words.ex: We went on an adventure in the woods.
words.ex2: The pirates in the story had a big adventure at sea.
words.nonExample: Sitting in a chair all day is not an adventure.

apps.academic: Write a story about an adventure.
apps.writing: Tell where the adventure was and what happened.

cloze.s: Tom packed a map and a flashlight for his cave ___.

cloze2.s: The brave mouse set off on an ___ across the wide river.

misuse.s: A nap in my bed was a dangerous adventure across the sea.
misuse.why: An adventure is an exciting trip. A nap in bed is quiet and safe.

visual.alt: A compass beside a mountain and a river.

words.def: Something you learn from a story or from doing.
words.ex: The story taught a lesson about sharing.
words.ex2: I learned a lesson when I forgot my coat.

senses.def: A class where a teacher teaches.
senses.example: Our piano lesson is on Friday.

apps.academic: What lesson did the character learn?
apps.writing: Tell the lesson at the end of your story.

cloze.s: The tortoise won the race, and the ___ was to never give up.

cloze2.s: Sam missed the bus once, so he learned the ___ of leaving early.

misuse.s: The lesson was a red balloon that Ana held.
misuse.why: A lesson is something you learn. A balloon is a thing you hold.

visual.alt: An open book with a light bulb above it.

words.def: Make a picture of something in your mind.
words.ex: Close your eyes and imagine a purple dragon.
words.ex2: Can you imagine a house made of ice?

apps.academic: Imagine a new ending for the story.
apps.writing: Use imagine to start a make-believe story.

cloze.s: Close your eyes and ___ a castle floating in the clouds.

cloze2.s: Can you ___ what it would be like to fly like a bird?

misuse.s: I imagine my lunch by looking at it on my desk.
misuse.why: To imagine is to picture something in your mind. Looking at a real lunch is seeing, not imagining.

visual.alt: A thought bubble with a dragon inside.

passage.title: Leo's Kite
paras: The setting was a windy beach, and Leo had a new kite. Then the string broke, and the kite flew away! This event became an adventure. Leo ran fast until he caught the string. His solution was to wrap it around his hand. The lesson was to hold on tight, and he could imagine his kite soaring.

qs.q: What is the setting of the story?
qs.why: The first sentence says the setting was a windy beach.

choices: He wrapped the string around his hand.
qs.why: After he caught the string, his solution was to wrap it around his hand.

qs.q: What is the lesson of the story?
qs.why: The story says the lesson was to hold on tight.

write.prompt: Draw the setting for your own story. Tell or write who is there and what happens.
write.frame: The setting is ___. An event is ___.

study.task: Clap the beats in each word: set-ting, e-vent, so-lu-tion, ad-ven-ture, les-son, i-mag-ine. Which words have three beats?

sentences: Say the setting of a story you know.
Write one event from a story you read.
Tell a solution to a problem in a story.

given: The class went on a trip.
combine.model: The class trip was an exciting adventure.

given: She learned to check her bag.
combine.model: Mia learned a lesson when she lost her coat.

discuss: What is the best adventure you have heard in a story?
What can you imagine at the end of a rainbow?
produce.explain: Explain the lesson of a story you know. Use because.

constructed.prompt: Tell the setting and one event of a story you know.
constructed.model: The setting is a farm in spring. One event is when the pig runs away.

constructed.prompt: Tell a problem in a story. Then tell the solution and the lesson.
constructed.model: The problem was a lost kite. The solution was to hold the string tight. The lesson was to be careful.

teacher.overview: Children learn six words for how a story is built and what it teaches, then use them to talk about a short story. The unit revisits then, finally, and happen.

notes.va.setting.n: Setting is where and when. Show a picture and ask 'Where are we? What time of year?' Do not confuse it with the character.
notes.va.event.n: An event is something that happens. Use a three-event picture strip. Link to the word happen from the cause unit.
notes.va.solution.n: Solution fixes a problem. Pair it with a problem card: a lost cat has a solution of signs. Solution is not the same as an answer to a question.
notes.va.adventure.n: Adventure is an exciting trip or story. Let children name an adventure they have read about. Keep it safe and imaginative.
notes.va.lesson.n: A story lesson is what a character learns. Do not mix it up with a school lesson; the second sense is in the senses list.
notes.va.imagine.v: Say 'Close your eyes and imagine' with a prompt. Imagine is pictures in the mind, not seeing a real thing.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'In this story, the setting is a dark forest. The first event is that the bear finds a boat. Then the boat leaks, which is a problem. The solution is to patch it with leaves. The lesson is to think before you act. I can imagine a different ending, too.'
discuss: What is the setting of a story you like?
What lesson did a character learn?
misconceptions: A lesson is only a school class.
extend: Children retell a story using setting, event, solution, and lesson on four index cards.
Children draw their own adventure in four boxes and tell it to a partner.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit setting, event, and solution the next day with a new read-aloud, again at one week, and use them when children retell any story. They return when children study characters in unit 11.

wida.oral: Partner A tells a short story in four sentences. Partner B names the setting, one event, the solution, and the lesson.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (ambiente, evento, solución, aventura, lección, imaginar) are not reviewed by a native speaker; setting also appears as escenario in school texts.
Lesson carries a second sense (a class) in senses; the unit teaches the story-lesson sense.
